title: Set localization of a left proper combinatorial model category without simplicial enrichment
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the model-category and combinatorial terminology of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Let $\mathcal N$ be a left proper combinatorial model category with functorial factorizations; left proper means that pushout along a cofibration preserves weak equivalences. Let $S$ be a small set of maps of $\mathcal N$. Write $\operatorname{Map}^h$ for homotopy function complexes in the original model, equivalently the mapping spaces in its homotopy coherent localization, as in [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]. A fibrant object $Z$ is $S$-local if $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. A map $u:X\to Y$ is an $S$-equivalence if $\operatorname{Map}^h(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence for every fibrant $S$-local $Z$.

There is a left proper combinatorial model structure $L_S\mathcal N$ on the same category, with the original cofibrations, the $S$-equivalences as weak equivalences, and the original fibrant $S$-local objects as fibrant objects. Its two model factorizations can be chosen functorially, so it also has functorial fibrant replacement. The identity $\mathcal N\to L_S\mathcal N$ is left Quillen. For any model category $\mathcal T$ and Quillen adjunction $F:\mathcal N\rightleftarrows\mathcal T:G$, if the total left derived functor $LF$ carries every member of $S$ to an isomorphism in the homotopy category of $\mathcal T$, the same underlying adjunction is Quillen from $L_S\mathcal N$ to $\mathcal T$. Here the homotopy category is the ordinary localization at weak equivalences. No simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal N$ or $\mathcal T$ is assumed. A Quillen adjunction means that its left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations; a trivial cofibration is a cofibration that is also a weak equivalence.

source.place: Barwick, On left and right model categories and left and right Bousfield localizations, Definition 4.2, Theorem 4.7 and its proof, printed pp. 42-44; functorial small-object factorizations for the combinatorial model. Read online 2026-10-17; absent from local literature. No Stacks tag states this model-category theorem.

proof.text: Write $W_0,C$ for the old weak equivalences and cofibrations, and $W$ for the $S$-equivalences in the statement. The old localization sends every $W_0$-map to an equivalence, so its mapping spaces send it to equivalences; hence $W_0\subseteq W$. The definition of locality also gives $S\subseteq W$. Precomposition into any fixed local object respects identities and composition; equivalences of spaces satisfy two-out-of-three and are retract closed. Testing separately at every fibrant local object therefore shows that $W$ contains isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three, and is retract closed. Locality is invariant under old weak equivalences between old fibrant objects, since the corresponding maps of derived mapping spaces are equivalences.

source.place: Definition 4.2 and the first verification in Theorem 4.7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-homotopy-local-equivalences-accessible] to the original combinatorial model and the given small set $S$. It says precisely that this $W$ is a replete accessible full subcategory of the ordinary arrow category, closed under sufficiently filtered colimits in that arrow category. This establishes the accessibility hypothesis of Smith recognition before any localized model structure is constructed. No enrichment, cofibrant endpoints, or already existing localization is used.

The class $C$, as a left diagonal-lifting class, contains isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts and retracts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]; [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] gives closure under all small continuous transfinite compositions. Choose a small old generating set $I$ of cofibrations, so $I^{\square}$ is the old trivial fibrations. The accessible small-object factorization writes any $c:A\to B$ in $C$ as $p a$, with $a$ in the weak saturation of $I$ and $p\in I^{\square}$. Lift $c$ against $p$ in the square with top $a$ and bottom $1_B$: the resulting $h:B\to\operatorname{cod}(a)$ has $hc=a$ and $ph=1_B$. Thus $c$ is an arrow retract of $a$. The reverse containment holds because $I\subseteq C$ and $C$ is weakly saturated. Therefore $C$ is weakly saturated and small-generated, exactly as Smith recognition requires.

source.place: Theorem 4.7, choice of generating cofibrations; Proposition 2.2 and small-object/retract argument.

proof.text: The intersection $C\cap W$ is closed under pushouts. Indeed if $i:A\to B$ belongs to it and $A\to X$ is arbitrary, [lem-cbc-left-proper-derived-cell-colimits](a) identifies mapping out of $B\amalg_A X$ into a local fibrant $Z$ with the homotopy pullback of $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$. The first map is an equivalence, so restriction to $\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence. The pushout map is therefore in $W$, and it is in $C$ by step 3. For a small continuous transfinite chain of maps in $C\cap W$, prove by transfinite induction that the map from its initial stage to each stage is in $W$. The successor case is composition. At a nonzero limit, the diagram consists of cofibrations by step 3, and part (b) of the same cell-colimit node identifies the derived mapping space of the colimit with the homotopy limit of the earlier mapping spaces. By the induction hypothesis the restrictions give an objectwise equivalence from this diagram of spaces to the constant diagram with value $\operatorname{Map}^h(X_0,Z)$. The opposite ordinal has terminal object $0$, and the maps to $0$ give a contraction of its nerve. Thus the homotopy limit of that constant diagram is $\operatorname{Map}^h(X_0,Z)$, with evaluation at $0$ as the equivalence. Taking limits of the objectwise equivalence proves the required restriction equivalence at the limit. The zero stage is the identity. Retracts and isomorphisms were handled in steps 1 and 3. Thus $C\cap W$ is weakly saturated. The comparisons explicitly allow noncofibrant initial objects and limits of every small cofinality.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.7, printed pp. 43-44; expanded continuous-chain limit verification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-smith-model-recognition] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal N$ and the classes $C,W$. Completeness and local presentability are part of the original combinatorial hypothesis. Step 3 supplies small generation and weak saturation of $C$, step 4 the weak saturation of $C\cap W$, step 2 accessibility of $W$, and step 1 two-out-of-three. Finally $C^{\square}$ is the class of old trivial fibrations by the old weak factorization system, so $C^{\square}\subseteq W_0\subseteq W$. Recognition produces a combinatorial model on the same category with cofibrations $C$, weak equivalences $W$, fibrations $(C\cap W)^{\square}$, and functorial factorizations. Call it $L_S\mathcal N$. Applying its functorial trivial-cofibration/fibration factorization to $X\to1$ gives functorial fibrant replacement.

To check new left properness, push out $f:X\to Y$ in $W$ along $c:X\to X'$ in $C$. Factor $f=p i$ in the old model with $i:X\to E$ a cofibration and $p:E\to Y$ an old trivial fibration. Since $p\in W_0\subseteq W$, two-out-of-three gives $i\in C\cap W$. Put $E'=E\amalg_X X'$. By step 4, $X'\to E'$ is in $W$. The map $E\to E'$ is the pushout of $c$, so is an old cofibration. Old left properness, applied to $p$ along this map, shows $E'\to Y\amalg_E E'$ is in $W_0\subseteq W$. The pushout universal property identifies $Y\amalg_E E'$ with $Y\amalg_X X'$ and the composite with the pushed-out $f$. Composition proves the claim. The identity preserves $C$ and old trivial cofibrations, since $W_0\subseteq W$, so it is left Quillen. Both models have the same trivial fibrations, namely $C^{\square}$, and the same cofibrant objects.

source.place: Theorem 4.7, left properness and identity adjunction, expanded directly from the two model structures.

proof.text: A new fibrant $Z$ is old fibrant, since it lifts against all new trivial cofibrations, which include all old ones. Choose old cofibrant replacements $QX\to X$ and old cosimplicial frames on $QX$. These replacements are also new trivial fibrations by step 6; the frames have the same latching cofibrations and their augmentation equivalences lie in $W_0\subseteq W$, so they are also new frames. Apply [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] separately in the two models. The identical Kan complexes $\operatorname{Hom}((QX)^\bullet,Z)$ compute the old and new derived mapping spaces into $Z$, naturally in $X$ and restriction maps. Every $s\in S$ lies in $W$ by step 1, so it induces an equivalence of the new mapping spaces into $Z$, and hence of the old ones. Therefore every new fibrant object is old fibrant and $S$-local.

source.place: Theorem 4.7(4.7.4); agent expansion by comparison of old/new frames, using Barwick Scholium 3.64.

proof.text: First note that a $W$-map $u:U\to V$ between old fibrant local objects is in $W_0$. The category formed from components of the old localization mapping spaces is an ordinary localization: apply the coherent localization universal property to nerves of arbitrary ordinary categories. Thus its morphisms are those of the old homotopy category. On components of old derived mapping spaces, precomposition by $u$ is bijective for targets $U$ and $V$. The first surjectivity gives $g:V\to U$ in the old homotopy category with $gu=1_U$. The second injectivity, applied to $(ug)u=u=1_Vu$, gives $ug=1_V$. Thus $u$ is invertible there, and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] gives $u\in W_0$. Now let $Z$ be old fibrant local and factor $Z\to1$ in the new model as a new trivial cofibration $j:Z\to RZ$ followed by a new fibration. Step 7 makes $RZ$ old fibrant local. The observation just proved makes $j$ an old weak equivalence, and $j$ is an old cofibration, so it is an old trivial cofibration. Old fibrancy of $Z$ gives a retraction $r:RZ\to Z$ of $j$ by lifting against $Z\to1$. Hence $Z\to1$ is an arrow retract of the new fibration $RZ\to1$, and is a new fibration by retract closure of lifting classes. This proves the reverse fibrancy implication. No ordinary extension assertion was inferred merely from a derived mapping-space equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 4.7(4.7.4); agent expansion of the fibrant-object identification by Yoneda cancellation and a retract.

proof.text: Let $F:\mathcal N\rightleftarrows\mathcal T:G$ satisfy the hypothesis in the statement. For every fibrant $Y$ of $\mathcal T$, $GY$ is old fibrant. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to the original Quillen adjunction: the old derived mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}^h_{\mathcal N}(-,GY)$ are naturally $\operatorname{Map}^h_{\mathcal T}(LF(-),Y)$. For $s\in S$, choose an old functorial cofibrant replacement of its source and target. Its image under $F$ represents $LF(s)$ and is an actual map of $\mathcal T$. The assumption that this is invertible in the homotopy category implies it is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]. It therefore induces equivalences of all these mapping spaces. Thus $GY$ is $S$-local. This uses neither simplicial enrichment nor any combinatorial hypothesis on $\mathcal T$.

source.place: Definition 4.2(4.2.1); agent expansion of the universal-property verification deferred in the proof of Theorem 4.7.

proof.text: For an old fibration $p:U\to V$ between old fibrant local objects, factor $p=q a$ in the new model, with $a:U\to E$ a new trivial cofibration and $q:E\to V$ a new fibration. Step 8 makes $V$ new fibrant, so $E$ is new fibrant and thus old fibrant local by step 7. The observation in step 8 makes $a$ an old weak equivalence, hence an old trivial cofibration. Lift $a$ against the old fibration $p$ using top $1_U$ and bottom $q$, obtaining $r:E\to U$ with $ra=1_U$ and $pr=q$. This exhibits $p$ as an arrow retract of $q$, so it is a new fibration. Now $G$ sends fibrations between fibrant objects of $\mathcal T$ to old fibrations between old fibrant local objects by step 9 and the original Quillen adjunction, hence to new fibrations by this argument. It sends trivial fibrations of $\mathcal T$ to old trivial fibrations, which are new trivial fibrations by step 6. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-quillen-fibrant-test] for the same ordinary adjunction $F\dashv G$ between $L_S\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal T$ are therefore verified. That node makes it Quillen, establishing the claimed universal property without assuming the source of a new trivial cofibration is cofibrant.

source.place: Definition 4.2 and Theorem 4.7 universal property; retract argument and unenriched fibrant-object Quillen test.

tool_uses.why: Unenriched frames compute old/new derived mapping spaces and preserve their restriction maps; the compact-support unit has no replacement for this model-category tool.
Arrow retract and pushout closure for lifting classes; this is a generic category-theoretic tool, not a replacement for the compact-support route.
Transfinite closure of a diagonal-lifting class, used to check Smith small generation.
Functorial small-object factorization of the old generating cofibrations, used only in the small-generation check.
General combinatorial recognition theorem applied after checking every hypothesis; the unit supplies no model-recognition theorem.
Saturation of any model category, used for maps between local objects and for the derived-functor hypothesis.
Unenriched mapping-space adjunction and preservation of fibrations by the original right Quillen functor.
General test promoting preservation of trivial fibrations and fibrations between fibrants to a Quillen adjunction.
